name: Ritz Carlton Coconut Grove, Miami
positioning: Boutique-style Ritz-Carlton in Coconut Grove, Miami's oldest neighborhood (official name: The Ritz-Carlton Coconut Grove, Miami)
best_for: Travelers who want to explore Coconut Grove's history and nearby attractions
Guests who like a pool with cabanas and a garden restaurant
Families looking for a local art experience

facts.text: Coconut Grove is Miami's oldest neighborhood.
Every guest room and suite has a private balcony and floor-to-ceiling windows.
The suites have full marble bathrooms, separate living and dining areas, and oversized balconies.
The Sundeck is a cafe and bar at the pool where private cabanas can be reserved.
The hotel is near Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, a National Historic Landmark.
The spa offers facials that feature ESPA products.
Fitness center access is exclusively available to hotel guests.
Atala Atelier is a private, family-friendly art experience guided by a local Coconut Grove artist.
Into the Glades is a guided journey into the Everglades ecosystem.
Miami International Airport is the closest airport to the hotel.

highlights.text: The Mariner's Reserve experience begins with a sail on Biscayne Bay and ends with a chef-curated dinner at Isabelle's Coconut Grove featuring the guest's own catch.
The Barnacle, home of Coconut Grove pioneer Ralph Middleton Munroe, is the oldest home in Miami-Dade County still in its original location.
The Commodore is a classic cocktail bar with live music, named after Coconut Grove's Ralph Middleton Munroe.
Isabelle's Coconut Grove has a trellised outdoor garden terrace next to the dining room.
Isabelle's Coconut Grove is named in honor of Isabella Peacock, one of the neighborhood's earliest settlers.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
Valet parking is the on-site parking option, and it carries a daily fee.
WhataHotel notes limited beachfront access compared to Miami Beach hotels.
